stemMd: The student wants to emphasize a drawback of drone counts compared with boat counts while acknowledging that the two methods give similar results. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.label: A
options.textMd: A drone count of the nests on Skellan Rock costs roughly 4,000 euros, mostly for processing the images, while a boat count costs about 1,500 euros.

options.label: B
options.textMd: A drone count needs only about ninety minutes of flying, compared with about six hours for a boat count, yet in 2023 the two methods found nearly the same number of nests.

options.label: C
options.textMd: When the nests on Skellan Rock were counted by both methods on the same day in 2023, the boat count found 11,840 and the drone count found 11,910.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Although drone and boat counts on Skellan Rock found nearly the same number of nests in 2023, a drone count costs roughly 4,000 euros, compared with about 1,500 euros for a boat count.

explanationMd:
This goal has two parts, and a choice that meets only one of them, or a near-miss of one, fails. Split the goal before reading the choices:

1. **Emphasize a drawback of drones compared with boats.** The notes give two differences: drones are faster (an advantage) and more expensive (a drawback). So the cost is the only fact that qualifies.
2. **Acknowledge that the results are similar.** The 2023 same-day totals, 11,840 and 11,910, show this.

Only the choice that begins with *Although* does both: its opening clause concedes that the two methods found nearly the same number of nests, and its main clause lands on the higher cost of a drone count. The structure matters too: putting the similarity in the *although* clause and the cost in the main clause is what makes the drawback the emphasis.

Check each remaining choice against both parts. One compares the methods on time, which is a drawback of boats, not of drones. One gives the cost difference but never mentions that the results agree. One gives the matching totals but no drawback at all.

distractorRationale.b: This has the right shape, a comparison plus an acknowledgment of similar results, which is why it is the strongest trap. But the difference it emphasizes is speed, and drones are faster, so it presents an advantage of drone counts rather than a drawback.
distractorRationale.a: This states the real drawback, the higher cost, and compares it with boat counts. It fails the second half of the goal: nothing in it acknowledges that the two methods produce similar results.
distractorRationale.c: This supplies the matching same-day totals, so it covers the acknowledgment half of the goal, but it names no drawback of either method. With nothing about cost, it cannot emphasize what the goal asks it to emphasize.

accessibilityText: Using the six student notes about counting gannet nests on Skellan Rock by boat and by drone, choose the sentence that emphasizes a drawback of drone counts compared with boat counts while acknowledging that the two methods give similar results.

provenance.notes: Original item. All four options use the notes faithfully, so the item turns entirely on which one meets both parts of the stated goal.

independentSolve.workingNotes: The goal has two parts: a drawback of drones (4,000 euros against 1,500) and similar results (11,910 against 11,840). Only D does both. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave7-sat-rw-run1) reached the same answer: The goal needs both a drone drawback (cost, 4,000 vs 1,500 euros) and an acknowledgment of similar results. Only D does both, with 'Although'. A gives the drawback without the acknowledgment, B stresses a drone advantage, and C gives only the results.]

review.notes: Author's own solve and uniqueness check: Two-part goal. Drawback of drones relative to boats = cost (4,000 versus 1,500 euros); speed is an advantage of drones. Similar results = 11,840 versus 11,910 (a difference of 70, under 1 percent). Only the 'Although' sentence has both. The speed-plus-similarity sentence has the right structure but the wrong direction; the cost-only sentence lacks the acknowledgment; the totals-only sentence lacks the drawback. Re-solved from the stem and notes alone: same answer. Unique. Options were reordered after review to remove answer-position bias; ids and labels were remapped with the key.
